requirements.definition: At the rightmost parenthesis of an unlimited format item, format control reverts to its leftmost parenthesis; this does not affect changeable modes.

requirements.title: Complete format reversion target, repeat reuse, mode preservation, and slash-like positioning
requirements.definition: At the complete format right parenthesis, format control terminates if no further item exists. If another item exists, it reverts to the beginning of the format item terminated by the last preceding right parenthesis that is not part of a DT edit descriptor, or to the first left parenthesis if there is no such preceding parenthesis. A repeat before the reversion parenthesis is reused, reversion itself does not change changeable modes, and file positioning is as for a slash edit descriptor.

pending.complete-format-terminates-without-item: Internal WRITE(buf,'(I1)') 7 to character(len=1); expect exactly buf='7' and no further record.
pending.nested-group-reversion-target: Internal WRITE to character(len=3) rec(3) with format '("H",(I1,","))' and integer values 1,2,3. Expect exactly rec(1)='H1,', rec(2)='2, ', rec(3)='3, '. Records 2 and 3 prove reversion targets the nested group terminated by the last preceding non-DT right parenthesis, not the first left parenthesis that would re-emit H.
pending.no-preceding-parenthesis-fallback: Internal WRITE to character(len=2) rec(3) with format '("H",I1)' and integer values 1,2,3. Expect exactly rec(1)='H1', rec(2)='H2', rec(3)='H3', proving fallback to the first left parenthesis when no earlier parenthesized format item exists.
pending.dt-parenthesis-excluded-from-target: Deferred until DT defined-I/O is registered, with exact planned oracle: define a scalar derived type whose formatted DT output writes exactly 'D'; internal WRITE to character(len=2) rec(2) with format '(DT(9),I1)' and items dt_value,1,dt_value,2 must expect rec(1)='D1' and rec(2)='D2'. The right parenthesis in DT(9) is excluded, so complete-format reversion falls back to the first left parenthesis and repeats the DT output on rec(2).
pending.repeat-reused-on-reversion: Internal WRITE to character(len=3) rec(3) with format '("H",2(I1))' and integer values 1,2,3,4,5,6. Expect exactly rec(1)='H12', rec(2)='34 ', rec(3)='56 '. The second and third records prove that reversion to the parenthesis preceded by repeat 2 reuses that repeat specification.
pending.complete-reversion-modes-unchanged: Deferred until 13.8 sign modes are registered, with exact planned oracle: internal WRITE to character(len=2) rec(2) using format '(SP,(I2))' and integer values 7,8 must expect rec(1)='+7' and rec(2)='+8'. Reversion targets the nested (I2), so SP is not reprocessed on rec(2); the plus sign proves reversion itself did not reset the changeable sign mode.
pending.reversion-positions-like-slash: Internal WRITE to character(len=1) rec(3) with format '(I1)' and integer values 1,2,3. Expect exactly rec(1)='1', rec(2)='2', rec(3)='3', proving complete-format reversion positions the internal file as slash processing would.

requirements.title: A reused portion on complete format reversion shall contain a data edit descriptor
requirements.definition: If complete-format reversion occurs, the reused portion shall contain at least one data edit descriptor.

pending.reused-portion-with-data-descriptor: Internal WRITE to character(len=1) rec(2) with format '(I1)' and integer values 1,2; expect exactly rec(1)='1' and rec(2)='2'.
pending.reused-portion-without-data-descriptor-r: Negative WRITE with a nonempty I/O list and format '(I1,("X"))' using two integer items. The whole format contains data edit descriptor I1, so 13.4 p2 is satisfied for the nonempty list; after the first item is consumed, complete-format reversion for the second item targets the last preceding parenthesized format item '("X")', whose reused portion has no data edit descriptor and therefore violates p9 only. Control changes the single property by adding a data edit descriptor to that reused portion, e.g. format '(I1,("X",I1))' with the same two integer items; no other rule is intentionally varied.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review against the pinned J3/24-007 PDF, THREE ROUNDS: doc/source_audits/batch_136.json. This OPENS CLAUSE 13, previously unregistered. The reviewer re-read PDF p289-294, re-derived unit hashes rather than accepting the author receipt, and independently reconciled the accounting: the true movement is 2363 -> 2392, net +29, being 31 non-numbered units newly classified offset by two numbered deferrals. R1303 and C1302 were correctly left UNRESOLVED BUT ACCOUNTED because legacy fixtures already exist for them and registering a numbered rule with pre-existing cases structurally forces binding them, which a source packet must never do; a migration followup is recorded. Seven blocking findings were raised across three rounds and all closed: 13.4 p9 reversion was under-specified (nested-group target, no-preceding-parenthesis fallback, DT-parenthesis exclusion and the changeable-modes obligation were all missing); pending plans were placeholders rather than byte-exact specifications; 13.2.2 p2 was dispositioned permission despite carrying mandatory shall restrictions; C1309 omitted m, d and e. Two further defects were introduced BY the first correction and caught on re-verification: a plan that wrongly assumed record advancement for unlimited-item reversion, which Note 4 explicitly denies, and a negative that violated both p2 and p9 so could not isolate the rule it was filed under. The reviewer hand-verified all four exact record specifications against the source. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1946, no fixture bound, no compiler invoked.
